First, who's a casual?

Different dock. Every. Single. Day.

A casual is a longshore worker who hasn't been registered yet. There's no fixed spot and no fixed hours: casuals are dispatched shift by shift to whichever terminal needs hands — Terminal Island tonight, Long Beach tomorrow, a 3 a.m. start the day after.

6:30AM

The call

The dispatch board runs. Where you're going isn't known until it drops.

7:00AM

Find the gate

A terminal you've maybe never worked. Which gate? Where's the lot?

11:30AM

Break

You're behind a fence on the water, hungry, with a short window to eat.

5:00PM

Night board

Then it starts again — second shift, hoot owl, weekends. Day or night.

Shadow Hook is the one app they open to get through all of it.

Inside the app

Built for the waterfront.

These are real screens. Everything a casual needs from the moment the board drops to the ride home.

The Ports

The whole harbor, in your hand.

A sky view of San Pedro Bay with every terminal on it. Tap a dock and you get its story, its yard map, every gate with one-tap directions, and who from the crew is working it tonight.

  • Every dock in both ports, tappable
  • Gates with ➤ GO straight to them
  • Yard maps, rows and bays
The Wire & Dockets

Know the call. Log the shift.

The Wire reads the dispatch board live — what's dropping and where the call is likely to stop. After the shift, snap a photo of the job slip and Dockets logs it: the week's take, the hours, the climb to the next pay bump.

  • The dispatch board, read live
  • Scan a docket, or log it by hand
  • Weekly take and the pay ladder
Mayday & the Armory

Safety first. Gear second.

When something goes wrong behind the fence, Mayday puts the terminal's security line and the right people one tap away. And the Armory is the crew's own store: PPE and work gear from vetted makers.

  • Terminal security lines & live alerts
  • The numbers that matter, in one book
  • Hard hats, hi-vis, gloves and more
